newsitem.title: CHINA: China says dissident's Hong Kong escape illegal.
newsitem.headline: China says dissident's Hong Kong escape illegal.

text.p: China confirmed on Tuesday that veteran dissident Wang Xizhe had fled to Hong Kong, accused him of escaping the country illegally and said Chinese authorities were investigating the case.
"Concerning the question of Wang Xizhe, this is a case of illegally and secretly crossing the border," Foreign Ministry spokesman Shen Guofang told a regular news briefing.
"The judicial authorities are currently pursuing the legal responsibilities of Wang Xizhe and the plotters," Shen said, apparently implying that Wang had help when he fled China last week.

Wang, 46, one of China's most outspoken advocates of democracy for more than two decades, escaped across the border to Hong Kong just days after a colleague in Beijing was sent to a labour camp for three years.
He is reported to be seeking asylum in the United States.
"We hope that countries concerned will not have the slightest ambiguity in cracking down on illegal and secret immigration," Shen said.

Wang had been missing from his home in the southern Chinese province of Guangdong since last Tuesday, when fellow pro-democracy activist Liu Xiaobo was arrested in Beijing and ordered to serve three years in a labour camp.
Wang and Liu had penned a daring statement last month calling for freedom of the press and urging the impeachment of Chinese President Jiang Zemin.
Wang would be the second Chinese dissident to flee to the United States via Hong Kong this year. Activist Liu Gang fled to Hong Kong last May and then found asylum in the United States.
The British colony of Hong Kong returns to Chinese rule next year.
The report of Wang's flight abroad comes amid a renewed crackdown on China's tiny, struggling democracy movement.

Wang was paroled in 1993 after serving 12 years of a 14-year sentence for sedition. He has spent some 17 years in jail and labour camps beginning in 1974 when he was arrested for putting up a wall poster advocating democracy in China.
